summary: Investigate development problems with original execution evidence. Wombat now separates generated tool requests from execution outcomes, reads diagnostic tool returns on demand, and makes continuation and installation problems easier to resolve.
highlights: Read original failed, interrupted, declined or unknown tool returns with history read --tools. Scalar strings and typed text-part arrays use bounded fragments and continuation; returned bodies are not stored in the index.
Inspect operation conflicts with reason codes and sampled original positions instead of stopping at an unexplained insufficient result.
Keep generated function/custom-tool requests as dispatch observations. Execution outcomes come from result evidence, preventing false endpoint conflicts and fabricated successes.

Include explicitly locally owned unified-exec startup commands in predecessor analysis. Compare recorded argv without interpreting arbitrary shell; verified reads and expected failures retain separate checks.
Continue development investigations through the request, original error, later handling and final state before proposing a specific change and recheck.
Recompute configuration explanations using the baseline's original global or project scope unless explicitly overridden. Token and pricing accounting remain unchanged.

Receive field-specific continuation errors and a matching schema command. Installation distinguishes a compatible Wombat bundle from unrelated Codex Skill parsing warnings, avoiding repeated reinstallation.
knownLimitations: A returned tool body does not by itself prove success or failure. Known outcomes remain available separately from results that need interpretation; failures and repeated calls are not automatically classified as waste.
Conflict details are bounded samples and disclose completeness. Diagnostic text excludes unsupported non-text parts and reports partial content.

Timing responses now use protocol v8; the analysis method remains safe_event_turn_v7. Update the CLI, plugin and integrations together. Previous response versions are rejected without compatibility aliases.
Cross-turn task interpretation and recommendations remain Codex work over selected evidence. Current configuration alone cannot establish historical execution conditions.
